evidence.title: Vitamin D supplementation and fracture risk in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis: a randomised controlled trial
evidence.abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoporotic fractures are a major cause of morbidity in older women. We assessed whether daily vitamin D3 supplementation reduces fracture incidence. METHODS: 1,240 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis were randomised to cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily or placebo for three years. RESULTS: Fracture incidence did not differ between groups; serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D rose in the treatment arm. CONCLUSIONS: Vitamin D alone did not reduce fractures in this population.

evidence.title: Calcium and vitamin D for the prevention of osteoporotic fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.abstract: We searched MEDLINE and Embase for trials of calcium, vitamin D, or both, in adults over 50. Thirty-three trials were included. Combined calcium and vitamin D was associated with a small reduction in hip fracture; vitamin D alone was not. Bone mineral density changes were modest.

evidence.title: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and bone mineral density in older adults: a cross-sectional study
evidence.abstract: Low vitamin D status is common in older adults. In 3,012 participants, lower serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D was associated with lower bone mineral density at the femoral neck and with a higher prevalence of osteoporosis. Causality cannot be inferred from this design.
